title: Optimal Consumption and Investment with Energy-Efficiency Adoption
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework for analyzing consumption, investment, and energy-efficiency adoption decisions under uncertainty, introducing new definitions of rebound and backfire effects and integrating welfare implications into optimal subsidy design models. The authors formalize macro-level technology diffusion and energy consumption across heterogeneous agents, with numerical analysis based on a German single-family home case study.
key_points: Proposes a unified model integrating consumption, investment, and energy-efficiency adoption under uncertainty
Develops new definitions of rebound and backfire effects with welfare implications for subsidy design
Adoption threshold and post-adoption strategies depend on agent wealth, introducing financial conditions as a channel for technology-adoption decisions
Numerical analysis using a representative German single-family home case study
Results suggest adoption of energy efficiency is welfare-improving and subsidy policy can effectively steer aggregate energy consumption
Authors: Anthony Britto, Carlos Oliveira, Max Kleinebrahm
why_it_matters: This is academic research on welfare economics and energy policy rather than market structure analysis or macro catalyst identification. It does not address trading mechanics, market microstructure, liquidity, or market-moving event catalysts.
